newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends off sharply, then mixed on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends off sharply, then mixed on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures, pressured by forecasts for milder weather later this week, ended down sharply Thursday, then showed a mixed reaction to Wednesday's AGA storage report, sources said.

February tumbled 32.1 cents to close at $3.384 per million British thermal units, then climbed into the $3.40s and skidded into the low-$3.30s after weekly AGA data. March settled 24.8 cents lower at $3.00. Others also ended down.
"Initially, the AGAs were viewed as bullish, but there's no liquidity, so they sold it down later," said one Houston trader, adding mild weather forecasts pressured the complex.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 130 bcf to 69 percent of capacity, above expectations in the 110-120 bcf range. While overall stocks were still 86 bcf, or four percent, below year-ago, the report showed eastern inventories were 143 bcf, or 11 percent, above last year.

Technically, traders viewed today's action as bearish, citing a double top and an island reversal on the perpetual chart and February's close below the $3.47-3.475 gap. They saw next support in February in the $3.20 area, with psychological buying likely at $3.00. Resistance was pegged at today's gap at $3.595-3.61 and then at the contract high of $4.02.

In the cash, December Hub skidded more than 20 cents to the low-to-mid $3.50s, with January Hub talked in the low-$3.70s. December Midcontinent gas slipped a dime to the $3.55-3.60 area. New York city gate gas was talked in the $3.90s for December and in the $4.30s for early January. January baseload in NY was quoted in the $4.70s.
NYMEX said 19,895 contracts traded, down sharply from Tuesday's revised tally of 55,599.
